address: 288 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia (in the alley), Vo Thi Sau Ward, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: Legendary 60-year alley phở serving strict Nam Dinh/Northern-style beef phở with no herbs, sprouts or hoisin - the 'take it or leave it' bowl locals queue for.
dish: pho bo Nam Dinh (Northern-style, no herbs)

address: 435 Ly Thai To, Ward 9, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: North-to-South phở institution since 1954, famed for its giant 'to xe lua' (train-car) bowl of simple, garnish-free Northern phở bac that Saigonese have loved for 70+ years.

address: 25 Mac Dinh Chi, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: One of Saigon's oldest phở houses, founded 1947 by Mr Tran Van Phon and still simmering its crystal-clear, lightly sweet broth over a charcoal stove; now second/third generation.

address: 380 Nguyen Tri Phuong, Ward 6, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: The standout of District 10's neon-lit chè Thái street; a famously rich Thai-style sweet soup of pureed durian, jackfruit, palm seed and longan in coconut milk.

address: Huynh Man Dat, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: Cholon hủ tiếu Nam Vang run by a former cook for the Khmer royal family - one of the few places serving genuinely Cambodian-style Phnom Penh noodles in Saigon.

address: Vo Van Tan, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: One of Saigon's most storied hủ tiếu Nam Vang brands and reputedly its most expensive bowl - Chinese-Cambodian noodles with minced pork, liver, heart, shrimp and quail egg in a refined sweet broth.
dish: hu tieu Nam Vang (premium, with organs & shrimp)

address: 113A Dang Dung, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: The 'Commando Cafe' - a 1940s house that was a secret Viet Cong special-forces base with a weapons bunker and hidden mailbox; today it pours nostalgic bac xiu and serves com tam Dai Han above its wartime tunnel.
dish: bac xiu & ca phe sua da (secret-bunker commando cafe)

address: 207B Nguyen Van Thu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A perennially packed bún bò Huế spot beside the Conservatory of Music, singled out by a visiting New York chef as one of the best bowls of soup in all of Vietnam.
dish: bun bo Hue (Hue-style spicy beef noodle)

n: Banh Khot Co Ba Vung Tau
address: 40B Tran Cao Van, Ward 6, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: Saigon's best-known outpost of Vung Tau-style banh khot - crispy coconut-batter mini rice pancakes topped with shrimp - wrapped with herbs and dipped in sweet fish sauce; also serves banh xeo.
dish: banh khot & banh xeo (Vung Tau-style mini pancakes)

address: 277 Vo Van Tan, Ward 5, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A 40-year Chinese-Vietnamese street stall whose bot chien - rice-flour cake pan-fried crisp in a copper pan with egg, scallion and rich soy - is a Saigon late-afternoon institution.
